latest_release.body:
Memos 26.11.0 fixes typing Japanese and Korean in Safari and makes attachment failures visible instead of opaque. The server cache and upgrades from v0.31 deployment files are also more reliable.

## Fixes and polish

* **Editor:** Typing Japanese or Korean in Safari no longer selects the first word of a new line while the input method is composing. ([editor 26.11.0](https://github.com/usememos/memos/commit/c2f1699e031602fb5fcd8bad314120301e5f8009), [#6517](https://github.com/usememos/memos/issues/6517))
* **Attachments:** When an attachment cannot be read, the server answers with a JSON error instead of labelling it as the file's own type, so a PDF that fails to load no longer reaches the browser's viewer as a broken document. Missing local files return 404, and every failure is logged with its cause. ([#6516](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6516), [logged failures](https://github.com/usememos/memos/commit/3feb08737bfa831fdb6a4500bed8ec5e0cf257b6))
* **Server:** The in-memory cache keeps its entry count exact and no longer drops a fresh write when an expired entry under the same key is removed at the same moment, so it stays within its size limit under load. ([#6513](https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6513))

## Administration and integrations

* **Upgrading from v0.31:** Since 26.10.0, the deployment configuration files in `/etc/secrets` (`memos-idp-*.json`, `memos-instance-setting-*.json`) are no longer read. Startup now logs a warning naming any that are still present, so settings they used to provide, such as an S3 storage or an identity provider, do not revert silently. Move them into the configuration directory (`/etc/memos/config`) as described in the 26.10.0 upgrade notes. ([startup warning](https://github.com/usememos/memos/commit/83920cb3fbbdb8b85ec647968d5b0b802f3bd5e5), [legacy filenames](https://github.com/usememos/memos/commit/b40d8a7b573774c52b022c8d6537d6baf2129dc0), [#6515](https://github.com/usememos/memos/issues/6515))

## New Contributors
* @santhiprakash made their first contribution in https://github.com/usememos/memos/pull/6516

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/usememos/memos/compare/26.10.0...26.11.0

detail.readme_excerpt:
> ✨ Featured sponsor: [CodeRabbit — Industry-leading AI code reviews](https://coderabbit.link/usememos).

### Simple note-taking for your everyday thoughts. Memos is an open-source, self-hosted note-taking app that brings your everyday thoughts together in a personal timeline. Your data stays yours, and you choose what to keep private or share. [Demo](https://demo.usememos.com) · [Install](#quick-start) · [Docs](https://usememos.com/docs) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/tfPJa4UmAv) [![Docker pulls](https://img.shields.io/docker/pulls/neosmemo/memos?style=flat-square&logo=docker)](https://hub.docker.com/r/neosmemo/memos) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/usememos/memos?style=flat-square&label=Release)](https://github.com/usememos/memos/releases) ## About Memos Memos is an open-source, self-hosted note-taking app for your everyday thoughts. - **Everyday writing.** A single sentence can be a whole memo, or you can take your time with a longer entry, using Markdown to give your words more structure. - **A personal timeline.** Each memo stays with the day you wrote it, bringing your thoughts together in a timeline you can look back through. Tags connect related thoughts across those days, making it easy to pick up a topic again or find something you remember writing. - **Your own data.** Your record lives on your own server, and your data stays yours. - **Sharing you control.** You choose what stays private, what to share with family and friends, and what to publish on the web. In shared spaces, you can write alongside others while each person keeps their own memos. ## Quick start With Docker installed, run: ```bash docker run -d \ --name memos \ -p 5230:5230 \ -v ~/.memos:/var/opt/memos \ neosmemo/memos:stable ``` Open http://localhost:5230 and create the first account. Everything Memos keeps is in `~/.memos`, so back up that one folder. Other ways to run Memos, including Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and a plain binary, are in the [deployment guide](https://usememos.com/docs/deploy). ## Upgrading Releases are tagged `YY.MM.N`, with release candidates as `YY.
